title: The review parameter route, the by-number case path, the access decision and the field-level names of the review queue are not settled by the sources
source: RWB-E1-054 sections 3, 4, 5, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.1 (API-P5-006, API-P5-010 to API-P5-014); FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.10 and A2.11; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 16, 41, 42 and 44; split plan metadata of RWB-P5-E1054-APP
description: The legacy story reads four review parameters from document_hub_parameter, resolves the case in process through CaseDirectory, relies on the ACE common access check for the role, the team and the scope, and names the six endpoints and the two published Java interfaces in prose only. The target key is given DP-07 but not DP-06 or DP-08, its C list carries only RWB-P3-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1035-CON, and the plan lists no H row for the store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP although AC2 stores through it. No source states the production value of REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED, the field-level names of the queue, item, resolve, field-review and review resources, the text of MSG-P4-001, MSG-GEN-006 and the not-found answer, or the per-service login name, and the by-number case read the officer uses in step 5 is not restated in this key's sources: the path is the one RWB-P5-E1032-APP consumes under the same owner document.
evidence: RWB-E1-054 section 3 'REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED "DOC-SVC" (assumed), REVIEW_DATE_MIN 2000-01-01, REVIEW_DATE_MAX 2100-12-31, REVIEW_PAGE_SIZE 50'; section 4 step 5 'enters a case number that the system looks up through CaseDirectory'; section 10 'scope comes from the ACE common access check'; TSD P5 T-A.2 API-P5-010 'Response ReviewItemPage', API-P5-013 'Response IntakeResolution', API-P5-011 'Response IntakeItem' give no field list; split plan slice RWB-P5-E1054-APP carries C ['RWB-P3-E1043-CON','RWB-P3-E1035-CON'] and patterns DP01, DP03, DP07, DP09, DP11, DP13, DP15, DP19 with no DP06 and no DP08.
owner_role: Solution architect with the TechX tech lead of rwb-document and the P3 and P4 contract owners
proposed: Read the four review rows from document_hub_parameter in rwb_document and keep them data, publish the by-number case read on RWB-P3-E1035-CON so that both P5 keys consume one path, take the role, the team and the scope from the cached permission decision of the service template until a P4 CON row is added to this key, and let RWB-P5-E1054-CON fix the field-level names and the three platform message texts before the wave 1 entry check.

title: No source fixes the field-level names of the nine review resources, the one resolve answer, the field-patch idempotency, the document read position or the three platform message texts
source: RWB-E1-054 sections 7, 12, 13, 14 and 16; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1, T3.2, T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-P5-003, API-P5-006, API-P5-010 to API-P5-014); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16 and 42; split plan metadata of RWB-P5-E1054-CON
description: The contract baseline must publish seven operations, nine resources, one event, one record and five value sets, and no source fixes the field-level names of any of them. Three readings also have no single source: the legacy answers IntakeItem for SET_TYPE and DISCARD and Document for ATTACH while TSD answers IntakeResolution for the one operation; the legacy field patch carries If-Match and its AC17 requires an idempotent repeat while TSD marks idempotency not applicable; and the document read behind AC16 and behind a stored letter is the read of RWB-P5-E1024-APP, which this key declares as a reference so that one shape answers both. The idempotency stored-answer window, the texts of MSG-P4-001, MSG-GEN-006 and the not-found answer, the by-number case path and the per-service login name are likewise absent, and the three consumed rows are faked although the C list of this story is empty by rule.
evidence: RWB-E1-054 section 12 'POST /intake-items/{intakeItemId}/resolve | Response IntakeItem for SET_TYPE and DISCARD; Document for ATTACH'; TSD P5 T-A.2 API-P5-013 'Response IntakeResolution', API-P5-006 'Idempotency Not applicable'; RWB-E1-054 section 12 'PATCH /api/recovery/v1/documents/{documentId}/fields/{fieldId} | header If-Match with the document version' and AC17 'the response is 200 with the saved field And confirmed_by and updated_at are unchanged'; TSD P5 T-A.2 API-P5-011 'Response IntakeItem' with no field list.
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-document with the solution architect
proposed: Freeze the seven operations, the nine resources, the five value sets, the one IntakeResolution envelope, the If-Match lock with the idempotent repeat, the declared reference to the document read and the event schema in the rwb-document OpenAPI and AsyncAPI documents, keep the three platform message texts and the by-number path as recorded placeholders until their owners confirm them, and collect the consumer sign-off of the app story, the two screens, the store and extraction owners, the P3, P4 and P7 stories and the wave 1 harness.

title: The channel pickup has no target shape of its own: the run record, the rerun operation, the channel property layout, the single-run rule and the cross-service partner read are named by the legacy story only
source: RWB-E1-057 sections 3, 4, 8, 12, 13 and 14; TSD P5 v2 T-A.1 and T3.1; FSD P5 A2.13, A2.14 and A2.15; Arch v5 slides 11, 16, 41, 42 and 44; the plan metadata of RWB-P5-E1057-APP
description: The legacy story runs intakeStep inside a Spring Batch job on a shared Quartz scheduler and reads the job record from the same database. The target has no JOB-12 Quartz job, no job record table and no `admin/jobs` API family, so the run record, the three admin operations and the fields of the run answer are fixed by RWB-P5-E1057-CON and not by a source. The legacy intake container and the target hold container `rwb-quarantine` are not the same name. The channel properties, the branch codes, the folder names and the mailbox codes are environment values no source lists. The partner panel is read in process through PartnerDirectory in the legacy story and through the `rwb-partner` contract in the target, and the plan's C list carries only the two P3 contracts. The business-hours window, the holiday skip and the one-run-across-instances rule are stated by the legacy story alone and map to a Schedule overlap policy and a workflow ID. The five `document_hub_parameter` values are assumed under DL11. SCR-44 Interface and job monitor and its states belong to Epic 2.
evidence: Legacy section 12: 'Job name | JOB-12 Document intake; this story adds intakeStep as the first step' and 'Endpoint used: POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun'. Legacy section 3: 'The channels are set per environment by the platform administrator in properties'. Arch v5 slide 44 row JOB-12: 'every 15 min | rwb-document | event + KEDA workers'. Plan slice RWB-P5-E1057-APP carries C ['RWB-P3-E1042-CON','RWB-P3-E1043-CON'] only, and the app story consumes a partner read as well.
proposed: Publish the three admin operations and the run record in RWB-P5-E1057-CON, read the legacy intake container as the hold container `rwb-quarantine`, carry the channel property layout as environment values of RWB-P5-E1057-INF and RWB-P5-E1057-OPS, consume the partner read through the `rwb-partner` contract with a fake and no C row, and have the Schedule owner confirm the business-hours window, the overlap policy and the catch-up window before the wave 1 release.

title: The channel-intake contract baseline fixes operation names, shapes and enumerations the sources do not name, and the plan's C list omits the partner read
source: TSD P5 v2 T3.1, T3.2, T-A.1 and T-A.2; FSD P5 A2.13, A2.14 and A2.15; RWB-E1-057 sections 12 and 14; Arch v5 slides 11, 16, 41 and 42; the plan metadata of RWB-P5-E1057-CON
description: No source states the names of the three admin operations, the fields of IntakeRun, IntakeRunChannel or IntakeRunPage, the channel code pattern, the three run states, the three result classes or the four refusal reason codes; the legacy section 12 gives one rerun endpoint and a job record in prose. The not-found message text and the MSG-P4-001 text are not in the legacy section 14. The pickup event position is a negative, because Arch v5 slide 42 lists only DocumentStored and DocumentFieldsExtracted for rwb-document. The exact response field names of the partner-by-code read are absent and the plan lists no C row for it. The storage window of the idempotency key is a platform value the sources do not state.
evidence: TSD P5 v2 T-A.2 API-P5-013 gives 'Response | IntakeResolution' and no IntakeRun resource at all; legacy section 12 gives 'Request | Path jobId (uuid) of a failed JOB-12 run' and 'Response | Job' only; Arch v5 slide 42 rows 16 and 17 are the only rwb-document events; plan slice RWB-P5-E1057-CON carries an empty H, C, I and X list.
proposed: The baseline fixes the three operations and the three run resources as the smallest superset of the legacy job record, declares the channel code as a token and every list value as a list, publishes the six fakes and the drift test, and keeps every unnamed element behind the placeholder until the owner documents confirm it.

title: The four pickup channels, their credentials, their folder lifecycle, the partner DMZ position and the scan capacity are environment facts no source states
source: RWB-E1-057 sections 3, 4 and 13; FSD P5 A2.13, A2.14, A2.15 and A2.18; Arch v5 slides 11, 35, 38 and 44; NFR-004, NFR-052, NFR-053 and NFR-069
description: The legacy story names four channel classes and says the paths are properties; it names no branch code, no folder name, no mailbox code, no partner subfolder layout beyond 'one subfolder per partner_code', no host key or PGP requirement, and no scan rate. It assumes the mail service is Exchange Online read through Microsoft Graph with no open decision behind it. It assumes the intake container and the quarantine container are two containers, while the target names one hold container. Arch v5 slide 11 puts outside parties on MFT/SFTP with PGP and slide 35 puts partners behind the partner gateway in a separate DMZ, and no source says which of the two carries a partner evidence file. The scanning product and its provider are named nowhere. The replica counts, request and limit sets, storage budgets, clearing age, backlog threshold and scan rate are absent.
evidence: Legacy section 3: 'branch scanner folders by branch code, the mailroom folder, the partner SFTP inbound folder with one subfolder per partner_code, and the recovery mailboxes ... assumed to be Exchange Online read through Microsoft Graph (no open decision covers it)'. Arch v5 slide 11 File row: 'Blob + MFT/SFTP; PGP for outside parties'. Arch v5 slide 35 note: 'Partners: FAPI 2.0 ... separate DMZ gateway'. FSD P5 A2.18 names no scanner.
proposed: Record the channel inventory as environment configuration of the deployment, keep the partner key material and the mailbox credential in the key store as secret references, read the partner file path as the private MFT/SFTP route and the partner API path as the partner gateway in its DMZ, provision the scan capacity around the operation of RWB-P5-E1041-APP, and have the network and security owners confirm the DMZ position and the scan rate before the wave 1 release.

title: The deployment of the channel pickup has no source for its values, its chart key names, its Schedule ID, its catch-up window, its alert thresholds and its runbook entries
source: RWB-E1-057 sections 12, 13 and 15; Arch v5 slides 38, 42 and 44; the observability baseline of RWB-PLT-N005-OPS and RWB-PLT-E1056-OPS; the plan metadata of RWB-P5-E1057-OPS
description: The legacy story registers a Quartz cron and reads a job record from the database; the target registers a Temporal Schedule and reads a run record through the gateway-bff composite route. No source states the chart key names, the values layout, the channel block layout, the Schedule ID format, the business-hours window, the catch-up window, the alert thresholds, the lag threshold, the build ID format, the replica counts or the five runbook entries. The legacy alert set is MSG-P5-008 and MSG-GEN-006 only; a channel-not-ready text and an age-rule text have no identifier in the source set, and the attach-event lag alert has no identifier at all.
evidence: Legacy section 12: 'Trigger | Quartz cron `0 0/15 8-17 ? * MON-FRI` in Asia/Bangkok'. Legacy section 15: 'The platform administrator sees each JOB-12 run on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor'. Arch v5 slide 44 note: 'a Temporal Schedule (cron, with overlap policy SKIP and catch-up window)'. No source lists a chart key, a Schedule ID format or a runbook entry for this path.
proposed: Register the Schedule from the values of the release with the ID fixed by the release and an overlap policy of skip with a catch-up window of one run, deploy the four channel blocks as configuration per environment, publish the four alerts with their identifiers or their placeholders and one runbook entry each, and have the platform administrator and the Error and Message Standard owner confirm the window, the thresholds and the two missing identifiers before the wave 1 release.

title: The generation screens have no screen-read endpoint, the send path and the signature endpoint change owner, the lock flag and the three document states are in no list, and six consumed contracts sit outside the contract-dependency list
source: Legacy RWB-E2-017 sections 1, 3, 4, 9, 12, 13 and 14; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.1/T-A.2 (API-P5-014, API-P5-016, API-P5-017); TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (merge_field, signature_request) and T-A.1/T-A.2 (API-P6-009); FSD P5 Document hub v3 section 3 and A2.1; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.7; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 16, 41 and 42; ownership.json api and tables (document, document_type, signature_request, template, merge_field, treatment, recovery_case, decision_log_entry); work package B-P5-02 story line for RWB-P5-E2017-APP (H six rows, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON, I [], X RWB-PLT-TE012-APP)
section: 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.3 Events published; 12.7 Tables owned; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages; 15 Screens and states
description: Eight things this story needs are not settled by the sources. (1) The legacy flow shows a document set and a list of merge values on SCR-14 and SCR-30, but no endpoint exists for either read in the legacy section 12, the TSD P5 appendix or the API specification; only the generate, the regenerate and the review operation are named. (2) The send has two legacy names: section 13 adds POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents/send and section 12 declares POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/signature-requests, and in the target the second is P6's API-P6-009 (rwb-comms), so one of the two becomes a consumed operation. (3) The merge field catalog is said to mark each merge field overridable or locked, but TSD P6 T3.1 merge_field (DF-REF-252 to DF-REF-260) carries no such column, so the flag has no home in the target data model. (4) The document state values DRAFT, REVIEWED and SENT are the legacy values and no list enumerates them: TSD P5 T3.2 has no LOV-DOC-STATE and the standard column state is free text. (5) The set of template codes per treatment type and the three legal types CONTRACT, CREDIT_APPROVAL and MORTGAGE_DOCUMENT are assumed by the legacy story itself (DL28, DL19) and neither is enumerated in a source. (6) The write-once promotion of an already stored draft has no named operation: the store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP owns the row and the blob and the storage product RWB-PLT-TE012-APP owns the container, and no source names the call that moves a REVIEWED document to SENT with write_once true. (7) Six consumed contracts are in no C row: the P6 template catalog (RWB-P6-E1046-CON), the S2 treatment contract, the P3 case contract (RWB-P3-E1018-CON), the P7 ledger (RWB-P7-E1027-CON) and the P6 signature operation (API-P6-009), while the story's C list names the P3 reference-data contract only. (8) Four values this story needs are simply unstated: the per-service database login name, the two feature-flag names, the 24-hour idempotency parameter's access path and the texts of MSG-P4-001 and the not-found message. A ninth, smaller point is that the legacy story names no event of its own and the service has exactly two events in Architecture v5 slide 42, so the state change of this key is carried by the decision record and by nothing else.
evidence: Legacy section 13 reads 'Adds POST /documents/{documentId}/regenerate and POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents/send'; legacy section 12 reads 'POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/signature-requests (new, recorded in the additions file)' with the in-process interface package recovery.comms.signature; TSD P5 T-A.1 lists 17 endpoints and none is the set read, the merge-value read or the send; TSD P6 T-A.2 API-P6-009 is 'POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/signature-requests' with the Treatment and offer right C, declared as provided by RWB-P6-E2018-APP; TSD P6 T3.1 merge_field has id, merge_code, source_entity, source_field, field_id, is_required, personal_data, catalog_version and valid_from and no override flag; TSD P5 T3.2 lists LOV-CAPTURE-KIND, LOV-CUSTODY, LOV-DOC-SOURCE, LOV-EXTRACT-STATUS, LOV-INTAKE-MATCH, LOV-INTAKE-OUTCOME, LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW, LOV-OCR-STATUS, LOV-RETENTION-ACTION, LOV-REVIEW, LOV-ROUTE, LOV-SCAN-RESULT and LOV-STAGE and no LOV-DOC-STATE and no LOV-DOC-TYPE value row; legacy section 3 marks the template set RES-AGREEMENT 'assumed; DL28' and the three legal types 'assumed; DL19'; Architecture v5 slide 16 reads 'REST POST /documents (returns upload link) ... POST /documents/generate' and slide 42 rows 16 and 17 give rwb-document DocumentStored and DocumentFieldsExtracted only; the work package C list for this story is RWB-P3-E1043-CON alone.
area: Document (P5) generation screens: the missing screen reads, the send path and the signature ownership, the lock flag, the state values, the template set and the consumed contracts
owner_role: Solution architect, with the Legal counsel and product owner for the template set and the P6 and P5 service owners
proposed: Declare the set read and the merge-value read on base /api/recovery/document/v1 as this key's screen operations (ASM-102); keep the legacy section 13 name for the send, rebased as POST /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/generated-documents/send, and consume P6's API-P6-009 instead of providing the legacy signature endpoint (ASM-101); read the locked flag as a property of the P6 catalog answer and treat a field with no flag as locked (ASM-103); write DRAFT, REVIEWED and SENT as the three values of document.state and leave every transition to this story (ASM-104); keep the template set, the three legal types and the type mapping as data rows confirmed by Legal and the product owner (ASM-105); promote a reviewed document through the store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP and the storage product RWB-PLT-TE012-APP without naming a new operation (ASM-106); consume the P6 catalog, S2 treatment, P3 case, P7 ledger and P6 signature operations with fakes while the C list keeps the reference-data contract only (ASM-107); build the three signature-request operations that rwb-comms calls and mark their names as not specified (ASM-108); read GEN_IDEMPOTENCY_HOURS from document_hub_parameter, which is this service's own table (ASM-109); carry the D6.4 record as the only published element and declare no rwb.document event (ASM-110); rename the two flags (ASM-111); and carry the login name, the two message texts and the tentative release as placeholders (ASM-112).

title: The generation-screens baseline fixes six operations and four shapes that no source names, two conflicting legacy paths, the field names of the request and answer objects, and a status mapping the legacy section 12 states only in prose
source: Legacy RWB-E2-017 sections 4, 7, 9, 12, 13 and 14; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.1/T-A.2; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 and T3.2; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T5.3; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 16, 41 and 42; ownership.json api and tables; work package B-P5-02 story line for RWB-P5-E2017-CON (H, C, I and X all empty; ready Day 1)
section: 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.3 Events published; 12.8 Contract fakes; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages; 15 Screens and states
description: The baseline has to fix five things the sources leave open. (1) The operations: TSD P5 T-A.1 gives an API ID to API-P5-017 only, so the set read, the merge-value read, the send and the three signature-request operations are declared by this document with no identifier to copy, and the two screen reads have no legacy endpoint at all. (2) The paths: the legacy story names the send in its section 13 and a different signature endpoint in its section 12, and the second is rwb-comms's API-P6-009 in the target, so the document must state which one it provides and which one it consumes. (3) The shapes: the legacy section 12 gives RegenerateRequest and SendForSignatureRequest as a sketch and two page shapes as a name, and no source gives the field-level names of the set item, the merge value, the two pages or the signature request beyond the TSD P6 column list. (4) The values: the three document states are not in a list, the write-once rule is a business rule of the app story, the page size and the sort order are not stated anywhere, the 24-hour idempotency window is a parameter of the engine, and the element that carries a formatted value is this document's own construct. (5) The messages and the statuses: the legacy section 12 maps some failures to statuses in prose and section 14 gives the texts, while MSG-P4-001 and the not-found message are platform rows whose texts no story holds, and MSG-P5-012 is a confirmation and not an error. A sixth point is the event position: the legacy story names no event, Architecture v5 slide 42 gives the service exactly two events that are not this key's state change, so the baseline declares the decision record and must also state that neither of the two belongs to this key.
evidence: TSD P5 T-A.1 lists API-P5-017 'POST /api/recovery/v1/documents/{documentId}/regenerate | Documents U | E2' and no send, no set read and no merge-value read; TSD P6 T-A.2 API-P6-009 reads 'POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/signature-requests ... Response SignatureRequest[]' and is provided by RWB-P6-E2018-APP; legacy section 12 gives 'Request RegenerateRequest: overrides (array of mergeField, value, reason; 1 to 10), version (integer)' and 'Request SendForSignatureRequest: treatmentId (uuid), documentIds (array of uuid), header Idempotency-Key (required)' with no field list for the answers; TSD P5 T3.1 gives the document columns and TSD P6 T3.1 the signature_request columns (DF-DOC-096 to DF-DOC-107); TSD P5 T3.2 and TSD P6 T3.2 give the list values the shapes refer to and no LOV-DOC-STATE; Architecture v5 slide 42 rows 16 and 17 give rwb-document DocumentStored and DocumentFieldsExtracted only; the work package C list for this story is empty.
area: Document (P5) generation-screens contract baseline: the six unnumbered operations, the two conflicting paths, the unstated shape names, the parameter-driven values and the status mapping
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-document, with the solution architect and the rwb-comms owner
proposed: Declare the seven operations on base /api/recovery/document/v1 and map the regenerate to API-P5-017, recording that the other six have no identifier (ASM-113); declare the legacy section 13 send path and consume P6's API-P6-009, recording the legacy section 12 endpoint as the loser (ASM-114); fix the request and answer field names as the smallest superset of the legacy list and treat a later addition as additive (ASM-115); map every failure to one envelope and the statuses of the legacy rows plus the platform 401 and 404 rows (ASM-116); declare the decision record as rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 and state that this key declares no rwb.document event (ASM-117, ASM-118); declare the three state values with their meaning and no transition, leaving the request lifecycle to rwb-comms (ASM-119); and carry MSG-P4-001, the not-found message, the login name, the tentative release date and the Draft status as placeholders (ASM-120).

title: Field capture: the store capture block, the intake submit path, the parameter and list names, the service login name and the approval status are not settled by the sources
source: RWB-E2-024 section 3 and section 12; RWB-P5-E1024-APP section 12; RWB-P5-E1057-CON (not yet published); Ownership Map v1; TSD P5 T3.1
description: The legacy story sets five capture columns on the document itself and calls DocumentStore.store, a DocumentStoredListener and MalwareScanService.scanNow in process. In the target the document row has one writer (the store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP) and that store's request declares no capture block, so the block this story passes and the field names inside it are not named by any source. The intake item that the legacy listener creates comes in the target from the intake submit of RWB-P5-E1057-CON, whose path and shape are not published and whose owner document is not written yet; RWB-P5-E1049-CON declares a POST /intake-items of its own for the same effect, so two P5 baselines appear to declare the same creation path. The five parameter codes resolve to rows of document_hub_parameter whose names P5 owns, but no source names the parameter set the contract exposes. The list codes LOV-CAPTURE-KIND, LOV-DOC-TYPE, LOV-DOC-SOURCE and LOV-REVIEW are named by TSD P5 T3.1 but not resolved to their P3 admin paths for this story. The rwb-document login name, the not-found message ID and the MSG-P4-001 text are not named anywhere. The legacy status is Ready for build and no approval of the realigned story exists.
evidence: RWB-E2-024 section 12 'Idempotency | clientFileId unique per case' with 'StoredDocument DocumentStore.store(StoreRequest request)' and no capture block; section 13 'Flyway migration V2_5_024__field_capture.sql adds to document: captured_at ...'. TSD P5 T-A.2 API-P5-015 lists 'Request | Multipart: manifest, files' and no field names. RWB-P5-E1049-CON section 12.1 declares 'POST /intake-items'. Ownership Map tables: document, document_intake, document_hub_parameter, document_type = P5; parameter_catalog, reference_row, lov_value = P3.
proposed: The store of RWB-P5-E1024-APP takes an optional capture block (capturedAt, captureLatitude, captureLongitude, clientFileId, captureKind) as an additive change of its request within major version 1; the intake item for a bill and a checklist is created by the intake submit of RWB-P5-E1057-CON and RWB-P5-E1049-CON is read as the OCR pipeline that consumes the item; the five parameters are published by the P3 parameters contract under the legacy codes; the four lists are published by the P3 reference-data contract under the TSD codes; the story is Draft (realignment v1) and its release date is the legacy one and tentative.

title: Field capture contract: the manifest part and item field names, the stored-answer window, the not-found message and the 415 reading are not settled by the sources
source: RWB-E2-024 section 12 and section 14; TSD P5 T-A.2 API-P5-015; TSD P5 T3.1
description: The legacy contract describes the request in one prose row (a manifest JSON of inspectionRef and items of clientFileId, kind, capturedAt, latitude, longitude and fileName, with one file part per item) and the answer as FieldCaptureResult; no source fixes the part names, the exact property names, the required sets or the paging-free answer envelope, so the baseline must fix them. TSD P5 T-A.2 declares 415 for the operation while the legacy contract refuses a type per item at 201 with MSG-P5-001, so two sources disagree on where a type refusal sits. The stored-answer window of Idempotency-Key, the 404 not-found message ID and the MSG-P4-001 text are named by no source. The contract baseline is Day 1 and carries no build dependency, and its release date and approval status come from the legacy.
evidence: RWB-E2-024 section 12 'Request | multipart/form-data: manifest (JSON: inspectionRef, items of clientFileId, kind PHOTO, BILL or CHECKLIST, capturedAt date-time with offset, latitude, longitude, fileName) and one file part per item named by clientFileId'. TSD P5 T-A.2 API-P5-015 'Errors | 401, 403, 404, 413, 415, 422, 503'. RWB-E2-024 section 12 'Item-level refusals (MSG-GEN-002, MSG-GEN-003, MSG-P5-001, MSG-P5-016, MSG-P5-017, MSG-P7-003) do not fail the request; each is returned on its item.'
proposed: The baseline declares the manifest as one JSON part named manifest and each file part named by its clientFileId; the item properties are the legacy names with the required set clientFileId, kind and capturedAt; 415 is declared for a request whose content type is not multipart/form-data only, and a refused type stays an item with status REFUSED and MSG-P5-001 at 201; the Idempotency-Key window, the not-found message ID and the MSG-P4-001 text carry the placeholder until the platform catalogue fixes them; the baseline is Day 1 with empty dependency lists and a Draft status.

title: The checked-field reader, its operation and its field-level names are absent from every source, the five new types and the pass mark are an assumed load, and the case read of the scope check is in no C row
source: RWB-E2-025 sections 3, 7, 12, 13 and 16; TSD P5 v2 T-A.1 and T3.1; FSD P5 A2.22; Architecture v5 slides 16 and 42; plan metadata of RWB-P5-E2025-APP
description: Legacy section 12 publishes the Java interface DocumentFieldReader.checkedFields(UUID caseId, String documentType) returning a list of CheckedField with documentId, docVersion, fieldName, value, state and confidence, and no TSD P5 T-A.1 row, no Architecture v5 slide and no FSD P5 A2.22 flow names a REST operation, a path or a response shape for it. The operation, the path, the CheckedFieldSet shape and the field-level names beyond the legacy list are therefore open. The five new types and their fields are an assumed list of a DOCTYPE-2026.12 load that is signed off outside the source set (DL19), EXTRACT_ACCURACY_PASS 0.90 is an assumed value (DL11), the classifier version for the eleven types is selected through the agent runtime and named by RWB-P5-E1050-CON rather than by this story, and the plan lists only RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON as C dependencies while the scope check consumes the rwb-case case read.
evidence: RWB-E2-025 section 12: 'public interface DocumentFieldReader { List<CheckedField> checkedFields(UUID caseId, String documentType); }' and 'CheckedField: documentId, docVersion, fieldName, value, state (OK, CONFIRMED, CORRECTED), confidence'; TSD P5 v2 T-A.1 stops at API-P5-017 with no reader row; RWB-E2-025 section 3: 'signed by legal counsel and the Head of NPA (assumed list; DL19)' and 'EXTRACT_ACCURACY_PASS, assumed; DL11'; plan metadata of RWB-P5-E2025-APP carries C ['RWB-P3-E1042-CON','RWB-P3-E1043-CON'].
area: API contract, reference data and dependency list
proposed: Publish the checked-fields read on /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/checked-fields with the CheckedField and CheckedFieldSet shapes as the smallest superset of the legacy list, apply the assumed DOCTYPE-2026.12 load through the type table of RWB-P5-E1025-APP, keep EXTRACT_ACCURACY_PASS in document_hub_parameter, and confirm the operation and the field names with S4 and S2 before the wave 2 release.

title: The published Java reader becomes a REST contract no source names, the extraction operations belong to another baseline of the same service, and the plan lists no C row for the case read
source: RWB-E2-025 section 12; TSD P5 v2 T-A.1, T3.1 and T5.3; Architecture v5 slides 16, 41 and 42; plan metadata of RWB-P5-E2025-CON
description: The legacy interface is a Java call inside one process with a comment for its shape; the target makes S4 rwb-litigation and S2 rwb-treatment separate services, so the reader has to be a REST contract, and no source fixes its path, its resource names or its status set. At the same time the extraction operations of the same service are published by RWB-P5-E1053-CON, so a baseline that re-declared them would create two owners for one operation. The plan lists only the P3 parameters contract and the P3 reference-data contract as C dependencies of the app story, while the scope filter and the version rule consume the rwb-case case read and the type table version in force.
evidence: RWB-E2-025 section 12: 'The caller passes its own service identity; values are returned unmasked only to a module whose purpose needs them (SY-CASEWF, SY-AGENT), and never logged.'; TSD P5 v2 T-A.1 has no reader operation and T5.3 lists DocumentStored and DocumentFieldsExtracted only; the extraction operations are declared by RWB-P5-E1053-CON 12.1; plan metadata of RWB-P5-E2025-CON carries empty H, C, I and X lists.
proposed: Declare one checked-fields read on the service base as the baseline's own choice with its shape and status set, name the three extraction operations as consumed from RWB-P5-E1053-CON and re-declare none of them, keep the extraction event as the one declared event with the new type codes in documentType, and confirm the operation name with S4, S2 and the review queue before the baseline tag.

title: The deployment values of the extension are not specified: the model name and the provider product behind the agent route, the alert thresholds and identifiers, the evaluation cadence, the business-hours window and the reader thresholds
source: RWB-E2-025 sections 3, 7 and 13; Architecture v5 slides 16, 38, 42 and 44; FSD P5 A2.22 AC-BG-P5-022-01; TSD P5 v2 T7; Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-068 and NFR-052
description: The legacy story names a classifier version for the eleven types, a type table version and a pass mark, and leaves every operating value to the environment. No source gives the model name or the model version behind the agent route, the provider product, the alert thresholds of the extraction run and of the accuracy series, the identifier of the accuracy alert and of the reader alert, the cadence of the evaluation activity, the exact business-hours window of the intake Schedule, the latency and error thresholds of the checked-fields read or the alert routing roles. The OCR provider endpoint product is the intake release's and is verified here rather than set.
evidence: RWB-E2-025 section 3: 'The classifier version that knows the new types is trained on the sample and selected through the agent runtime (P10)'; FSD P5 A2.22 AC-BG-P5-022-01: 'Document intake | Schedule | Every 15 minutes'; Architecture v5 slide 44 JOB-12 gives the interval and no window; NFR-068 sets an alert duty and no threshold.
proposed: Ship every value as an environment value with the placeholder until it is confirmed, bind the model route endpoint and the client credential as a secret reference of the service identity, verify the OCR endpoint of the intake release without replacing it, and let the Error and Message Standard name the two alert identifiers before the wave 2 release.
